concepts.name: Newton's second law
concepts.statement: Particles move under the forces they exert on each other and any external fields: each particle's mass times its acceleration equals the force on it, m_i r̈_i = F_i(r_1, …, r_N).

concepts.name: Force field
concepts.statement: The forces on the particles, written as functions of all the particle positions, F_i(r_1, …, r_N), are known as a force field.

concepts.name: Trajectories from initial conditions
concepts.statement: Newton's equations for N particles are 3N coupled second-order differential equations; given the initial positions and velocities, their solution gives every coordinate and velocity for all time.

concepts.name: Temperature and kinetic energy
concepts.statement: The temperature is set by the average kinetic energy of the particles: (3/2)NkT equals the sum of ½m_iv_i² over the N particles.

concepts.name: Many microscopic states, one macroscopic state
concepts.statement: Specifying the trajectory of some 10²³ particles would take essentially infinite information, but the detail is not needed: enormous numbers of microscopic states give rise to the same macroscopic observable, such as the same temperature.

concepts.name: Ensemble
concepts.statement: An ensemble is a large collection of systems described by the same microscopic forces and sharing the same macroscopic thermodynamic variables, such as total energy, number of moles and volume, each evolving from a different initial condition.

concepts.name: Ensemble concept
concepts.statement: Macroscopic observables can be calculated by averaging over the systems of an ensemble; for time-independent properties such as temperature and pressure the average may be taken at one instant.

concepts.name: Thermal energy
concepts.statement: Boltzmann looked at temperature as a form of energy: the thermal energy of a system is directly proportional to the absolute temperature, E_thermal = kT.

concepts.name: Boltzmann constant
concepts.statement: The Boltzmann constant k (or k_B) is the proportionality constant between thermal energy and absolute temperature, and plays a central role in all of statistical thermodynamics.

concepts.name: Thermodynamic beta
concepts.statement: β is the reciprocal of the thermal energy, 1/kT.

concepts.name: Boltzmann factor
concepts.statement: The Boltzmann factor e^(−βE_i) of a state of energy E_i, with β = 1/kT, approximates the fraction of particles of a large system that are in that state.

concepts.name: Activation energy
concepts.statement: The activation energy is the energy a particle must carry to cross the energy barrier of an activation process.

concepts.name: Activated processes follow the Boltzmann factor
concepts.statement: The rates of many physical processes are set by the Boltzmann factor: the fraction of particles with enough energy to cross an activation barrier, such as escaping a surface, is about proportional to it, so a higher temperature sends more particles across.

concepts.name: Canonical ensemble
concepts.statement: The canonical ensemble holds N, V and T fixed: a collection of boxes of equal volume and number of particles, the whole collection kept in thermal equilibrium. It is the most practical ensemble.

concepts.name: Occupation number
concepts.statement: In an ensemble of A systems, a_j is the number of systems in quantum state j; the set a_1, a_2, … is a distribution.

concepts.name: Weight of a distribution
concepts.statement: The number of microstates that realize a distribution a_1, a_2, … of A systems over the quantum states is W = A!/(a_1!a_2!…).

concepts.name: Ensemble average
concepts.statement: The probability P_j that a system is in state j is the average of a_j/A over the allowed distributions, and any thermodynamic property is the average ⟨M⟩ = Σ_j M_jP_j.

concepts.name: Method of the most probable distribution
concepts.statement: A system tends toward the distribution of a_j that maximizes the number of microstates W, and with so many particles the fluctuations from the mean are immeasurably small, so the average distribution is this most probable one.

concepts.name: Constraints on a distribution
concepts.statement: A distribution must conserve energy, E_total = Σ_j a_je_j, and the number of systems, A = Σ_j a_j.

concepts.name: Method of Lagrange multipliers
concepts.statement: The method of Lagrange multipliers finds the local maxima and minima of a function subject to equality constraints by adding each constraint times an undetermined multiplier.

concepts.name: Stirling's approximation
concepts.statement: For large x, ln x! is approximately x ln x − x.

concepts.name: Probability of a state in the Boltzmann distribution
concepts.statement: Maximizing W while the energy and the number of systems stay fixed gives the most probable distribution, a thermally equilibrated distribution over all energy levels: the fraction of systems in state j is P_j = e^(−βe_j)/Σ_j e^(−βe_j).

concepts.name: Lower states hold more molecules
concepts.statement: In the Boltzmann distribution a state of lower energy always has a higher population than one of higher energy, and above absolute zero every upper level has a non-zero population however large the spacing; at higher temperatures more of the upper states are populated, each less.

concepts.name: Molecular partition function
concepts.statement: The molecular partition function is the sum of the Boltzmann factors over the states of one molecule, q = Σ_j e^(−βe_j); it is a number.

concepts.name: The partition function counts accessible states
concepts.statement: The molecular partition function indicates the average number of states thermally accessible to a molecule at the temperature of the system: the larger q, the more states the molecule can occupy.

concepts.name: Canonical partition function
concepts.statement: The partition function of the ensemble, Q(N, V, T), sums the Boltzmann factors over every state accessible to the system, counting every combination of the occupations of the molecules' states.

concepts.name: Partition function of distinguishable, independent molecules
concepts.statement: For independent molecules that can be told apart, the partition function of the system is the product of the molecular ones, Q = q_iq_jq_k…, which is Q = q^N when every molecule has the same states.

concepts.name: Partition function of indistinguishable molecules
concepts.statement: If the molecules cannot be told apart, q^N counts N! states too many, since N! is how many times the indices can be swapped without changing anything; the partition function is then Q = q^N/N!.

concepts.name: Average ensemble energy
concepts.statement: The average energy is each energy times its Boltzmann probability, summed: ⟨E⟩ = Σ_i E_iP_i = Σ_i E_ie^(−E_i/kT)/Q. It is the observed energy of the system.

concepts.name: Average energy from the partition function
concepts.statement: The average energy is a derivative of ln Q: ⟨E⟩ = kT²(∂ln Q/∂T) = −(∂ln Q/∂β).

concepts.name: Internal energy
concepts.statement: The internal energy U is the energy of the system, which statistical mechanics computes as the average ensemble energy.

concepts.name: Heat capacity at constant volume
concepts.statement: The heat capacity at constant volume is the change in internal energy with temperature, C_V = (∂U/∂T)_{N,V}.

concepts.name: Heat capacity from the partition function
concepts.statement: The heat capacity at constant volume is a second derivative of ln Q with respect to β: C_V = (1/kT²)∂²ln Q/∂β² = kβ²∂²ln Q/∂β².

concepts.name: Dulong–Petit law
concepts.statement: Dulong and Petit found in 1819 that solids have a heat capacity of about 2.49 × 10⁴ J kmol⁻¹ K⁻¹ near room temperature, explained by treating each atom as an oscillator with six degrees of freedom: C_V = 6R/2 = 3R.

concepts.name: Heat capacities fall toward zero at low temperature
concepts.statement: Experiment shows that the heat capacity of a solid decreases as the temperature approaches absolute zero, which the Dulong–Petit law cannot explain.

concepts.name: Einstein model of a solid
concepts.statement: Einstein treated a solid of N atoms as 3N independent oscillators: each atom moves in three dimensions within the lattice, the atoms do not interact, and all of them vibrate at the same frequency ν.

concepts.name: Einstein temperature
concepts.statement: The Einstein temperature Θ_E = hν/k writes the oscillator frequency ν of the atoms in a solid as a temperature.

concepts.name: Einstein heat capacity
concepts.statement: In Einstein's model the heat capacity of a solid is C_V = 3Nk(Θ_E/T)²e^(Θ_E/T)/(e^(Θ_E/T) − 1)², set by how accessible the vibrational energy is at the temperature T.

concepts.name: High-temperature limit of the Einstein heat capacity
concepts.statement: When the temperature is very large compared with the Einstein temperature, C_V ≈ 3Nk = 3nR, the value of Dulong and Petit.

concepts.name: Low-temperature limit of the Einstein heat capacity
concepts.statement: When the temperature is small compared with the Einstein temperature, C_V ≈ 3Nk(Θ_E/T)²e^(−Θ_E/T), which goes to zero with T, as experiment shows.

concepts.name: Stiff, light solids have low heat capacities
concepts.statement: Since ν = (1/2π)√(κ/μ), a solid with a high force constant or a low reduced mass, such as diamond, has a high Einstein temperature, and its heat capacity stays low until the temperature is high.

concepts.name: Where the Einstein model falls short
concepts.statement: Einstein's model fits the heat capacity of a solid at high temperatures, but at the lowest temperatures (below about 15 K for lead) it departs from experiment: the atoms of a real solid interact, which Debye's model takes up.

concepts.name: Pressure of a state
concepts.statement: The pressure of a system in state i is the negative change of that state's energy with volume, P_i = −(∂E_i/∂V)_N.

concepts.name: Pressure from the partition function
concepts.statement: The average pressure is a derivative of ln Q with respect to volume: ⟨P⟩ = kT(∂ln Q/∂V)_{N,β}.

concepts.name: Translational partition function
concepts.statement: The translational partition function of a molecule of mass m in a volume V is q = (2πm/h²β)^{3/2}V.

concepts.name: Gas constant
concepts.statement: R, the universal gas constant (8.314 J/mol-K), is Boltzmann's constant multiplied by Avogadro's number, N_Ak = R; it converts from a per-molecule to a per-mole basis, so Nk = nR.

concepts.name: Pressure as the energy change with volume
concepts.statement: A system pushing on a piston of area A exerts the force F = dE/dz; since A dz = −dV, the pressure is P = −dE/dV.

concepts.name: Classical canonical partition function
concepts.statement: For classical particles the canonical partition function is an integral of e^(−β𝓔(x)) over every point x of phase space, 𝓔(x) being the mechanical energy there; for N identical particles the integral carries the factor 1/(N!h^{3N}).

concepts.name: Canonical partition function of an ideal gas
concepts.statement: Evaluating the Gaussian integrals over the momenta gives the canonical partition function of an ideal gas, Q(N, V, T) = (1/N!)[(V/h³)(2πm/β)^{3/2}]^N.

concepts.name: Energies of independent molecules add
concepts.statement: The energy of a system of independent molecules is the sum of their energies, each molecule in its own state: E_l = ε_i^a + ε_j^b + ε_k^c + ⋯.

concepts.name: Distinguishable molecules
concepts.statement: Molecules are distinguishable when each can be told apart from the others, as the molecules of a crystal can be by the fixed sites they move around.

concepts.name: Two particles on two levels
concepts.statement: Two particles on the levels 0 and ε have four states if they can be told apart, Q = 1 + 2e^(−βε) + e^(−2βε) = q², but only three if they cannot, Q = 1 + e^(−βε) + e^(−2βε), which is not q².

concepts.name: When dividing by N! works
concepts.statement: Dividing q^N by N! counts the states of indistinguishable molecules only approximately, well when they rarely share a state, as in a large system with many accessible states; for two particles on two levels q²/2 is not the true partition function.

concepts.name: Average energy of a molecule
concepts.statement: The average energy of a single particle is its energies weighted by their Boltzmann probabilities, ⟨ε⟩ = Σ_i ε_ie^(−ε_i/kT)/q.

concepts.name: Average energy of independent molecules
concepts.statement: For N independent, indistinguishable molecules the average energy is N times that of one molecule: ⟨E⟩ = NkT²(∂ln q/∂T)_V = N⟨ε⟩.

concepts.name: Energy of a molecule by degree of freedom
concepts.statement: The energy of a molecule is the sum of the energies of its degrees of freedom: ε = ε_trans + ε_rot + ε_vib + ε_elec.

concepts.name: Molecular partition function as a product
concepts.statement: Because the energy of a molecule is a sum over its degrees of freedom, its partition function is the product of theirs: q = q_trans q_rot q_vib q_elec.

concepts.name: Partition function of a degree of freedom
concepts.statement: Each degree of freedom has its own partition function, a sum of Boltzmann factors over its states such as q_vib = Σ_i e^(−ε_i/kT), and its own average energy, ⟨ε_vib⟩ = kT²∂ln q_vib/∂T = −∂ln q_vib/∂β.
